report:
**Conclusion:** Yes, denosumab (Prolia) significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures in postmenopausal osteoporosis.

### Key Evidence
* **Pivotal Clinical Trial:** The primary evidence comes from the 3-year FREEDOM trial of 7,868 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. Subcutaneous denosumab (60 mg every 6 months) reduced the incidence of new morphometric vertebral fractures by **68%** compared with placebo (p < 0.0001) (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22095631/).
* **Mechanism & Broad Protection:** Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody targeting RANKL, a key protein in osteoclast development. By inhibiting bone resorption, it increases bone mineral density (BMD) at the spine and hip, additionally lowering the risk of nonvertebral and hip fractures (https://www.aafp.org/afp/2019/0501/od1).
* **Important Considerations:** Evidence indicates that the protective benefit depends on treatment continuity. Stopping denosumab leads to a rapid decline in BMD and an increased risk of rebound vertebral fractures, so clinical guidelines recommend transitioning to another antiresorptive agent (e.g., a bisphosphonate) if treatment is discontinued (https://www.ccjm.org/content/87/6/337).

### Sources
1. *The New England Journal of Medicine*: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493
2. *American Family Physician*: https://www.aafp.org/afp/2019/0501/od1
3. *PubMed*: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22095631/
4. *Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine*: https://www.ccjm.org/content/87/6/337
